title: Session History's 'Refresh history' toolbar action is enabled while disconnected and produces no perceptible change, unlike every other dead action in the app
what_happened: With no server paired, Session History correctly shows 'Connect to a server / Session replay requires the phone to be paired with a Skotiq server.' But the AppBar's 'Refresh history' button stays enabled. Tapping it runs _refresh -> _loadMore, which immediately hits `if (backend is! NetworkBackend)` and re-sets the same _LocalBackendNotSupported error, re-rendering an identical screen. No spinner, no SnackBar, no change of any kind. I tapped it and both the a11y tree and the screen were byte-identical before and after. The app disables dead controls correctly everywhere else on this dashboard - the Sequencer's Start and Stop both dump as [DISABLED], and the Log tab's 'Clear log' dumps as [DISABLED] - so this one enabled-but-inert action is inconsistent with the app's own established convention.
expected: Disable the refresh action when the backend is not a NetworkBackend, exactly as Start/Stop/Clear log already do, so `tree` reports [DISABLED] and a gloved 2am tap does not go unanswered.
repro: 1. Companion UI enabled; Skip Connection. 2. AppBar overflow 'More' -> 'Session history / replay'. 3. `drive_android.py tree` and note the screen. 4. `drive_android.py tap 'Refresh history'`. 5. `drive_android.py tree` again.

title: No single 'safe the rig' action: at 2am with clouds coming in, stopping the run and parking the mount are on two different tabs with no shared shortcut
what_happened: The companion is the surface you hold when you are in bed and the sky turns. The two things you need in that moment - stop the sequence and park the mount - live in two separate bottom-tab destinations with no common entry point. Stopping means: Sequencer tab, then press-and-hold the Stop button. Parking means: switch to the Mount tab, then reach _ControlsRow, which is the FOURTH child of that tab's ListView (after _PositionCard, _SlewRateSelector and the _Dpad), so on a phone it is below the fold and needs a scroll first. That is a minimum of tab-switch + scroll + tap, with a tab switch in the middle, and nothing anywhere in the persistent chrome offers 'stop and park'. The AppBar has room - it currently carries only a battery percentage, a network dot and a 2-item overflow menu whose contents (Saved servers, Session history) are both cold-path.
expected: A single persistent 'Safe the rig' affordance reachable from every tab - press-and-hold, destructive styling, one gesture - that stops the sequence and parks the mount in the correct order. Put it in the AppBar action slot or as a FAB. The press-and-hold pattern the Stop button already uses is the right interaction for this (it survives a pocket tap); it just needs to be reachable without first navigating to the right tab.
repro: 1. Companion UI enabled; Skip Connection. 2. Note the AppBar actions on any tab: battery '100%' at [678,165][828,238] and 'More' at [954,139][1080,265]. 3. Open More: only 'Saved servers' [471,170][1059,296] and 'Session history / replay' [471,296][1059,422]. 4. Sequencer tab: the Stop control is `Button: Press and hold to stop the sequence / Stop [DISABLED] [551,2012][1038,2127]` - present only on this tab. 5. Mount tab with no mount: only the empty state renders.
proposed_fix: Add a third AppBar action - a red shield/park glyph - wired to a press-and-hold that calls sequencer stop then mount park, with a confirmation toast naming both outcomes. Failing that, promote Park into _PositionCard so it is above the fold on the Mount tab and costs one tab-switch plus one tap.
